messages.text: where is the video for the hs15

I don't have a video link I can point you to for the H15 Dual, and I won't send one I haven't verified. What did you want to see — the noise level, or the dual-unit build? I can tell you either straight out. The H15 is $999, ships mid-November, and the drop date isn't announced yet.
how is the mining interface? since the 1373 chips and the scrypt chips are separate, can you assign 4 different sha256 pools, and 4 different ones on the scrypt side as well? or 4 pools total?

Honestly, I don't know the slot count. What I can tell you for sure is Harlo OS does pool mining — stratum URL, worker and password in settings — but how many pool entries you get, and whether the two chip sides get their own set, I won't guess at.

Let me put that to JD, who answers the hardware.
Handed to the team · Pool-slot count per algorithm on the H15 Dual / Harlo OS is not in the product f

JD has it and will come back to you right here — stay in the chat if you can, and if you step away the answer comes by email. Usually within one business day.

While you wait: is the dual-algo side the reason you're looking at the H15, or is it the BM1373 hashrate?
dual-algo
Read the hammer miner scrypt dogecoin litecoin page
Read the magic miner 40t page

Both algos today means two boxes, and honestly that's the route I'd take anyway — separate pools, separate failure. Magic Miner 40T, $799, 40 TH/s SHA-256 on the BM1370, and the Hammer DC02 at $239.99 does 105 MH/s scrypt on 25 watts.

Where would they run, and roughly what do you pay per kWh?

i have a dg home 1 at 370 watts, and 3 differnet sha256 miners at about 100 watts each. hs15 could replace all 4, and us 200 watts less. that is a neat thing, I just need to know how many algo it can do at once to split up the hashrate, and mirror what mine do now

That's exactly the question JD has — 4 pools total or 4 per algo. I've added your setup to it so he answers the consolidation, not just the spec.

One thing worth knowing now: the H15 isn't buyable yet. The drop date hasn't been announced, and the page reads ships mid-November. Want me to put you on the notify list?
i am already on the notify list. it would be neat to see something like the hs15 with a 140mm fan configuration

Big slow fan, less noise — yeah. I'll pass that to JD with the pool question; product feedback from someone running four units lands well with them.

For quiet today the Magic Miner 40T is the one: dual fan and heatsink, about 50 dB in Eco at 30 TH/s. Is noise the reason you'd consolidate?
mainly power to hash is my goal. 999 is  a lot of money to save 200 watts

Agreed, and I won't push it. 200 watts saved is about 144 kWh a month — at most home rates that's twenty-odd dollars, so $999 takes years to earn back.

If power-to-hash is the goal, the Magic Miner 40T is the better math: ~16 J/TH at 40 TH, ~15 in Eco. What are your three SHA units doing per terahash?
5 th, i have them scaled back to save power

20 J/TH. The Magic Miner in Eco is 15 — so for 150 more watts than your three combined you go from 15 TH to 30 TH, and every watt works 25% harder.

$799, Batch 6, ships November 14. Want me to build that cart?

nah. i'm going to leave this window open, so you can reply when you get an answer on the algo limit. I know 8 or 10 is the limit in testing, so the hs15 with 6 would be a good idea, you could use 4 for sha256, and the other 2 to split the scrypt side solo and pps. merge mine pools allow you to get a lot of coins on scrypt.
Used the chat-interview skill

Will do — window stays open, and JD's answer lands right here.

Before you go, one thing: you've got four units running and scaled back already. What made you start pulling them down on power instead of just running them flat out?
i have no job, income is very limited. i can't run everything balls to the wall without money coming in

That makes sense, and I'm not going to push $999 of hardware at you. Running what you've got, dialled back, is the right call.

Before you go: if that changes down the road, is it the power draw or the upfront cost that decides it for you?
i try to run everything the most efficient hash per watt. and of course the lowest cost hardware is a huge factor. don't skip on quality though, stuff has to last to get to roi

Fair, and that's three for three on efficiency, price and build. Noted for JD too — he likes hearing that from someone actually running units.

Nothing else from me. JD's answer on the pool slots comes back to this window.
off to mow the, tell abel mike jd and george I appreciate them ((contact hidden)) and happy hump daaaay! Thank you Sarah appreciate you too.

I'll pass that along to all of them, Ty. Happy hump day to you too.

Enjoy the mowing — JD's answer on the pool slots will be here when you're back in.
still waiting

Still with JD — it's with the team and the answer comes back here or by email, usually within one business day. They're on until 6 ET today.

I won't guess at the number in the meantime; a pool-slot count I made up is worse than waiting.
